title: Neutron Star
body:
A **neutron star** is what remains after a core-collapse [[Supernova]] when the core is between
roughly 1.4 and 3 solar masses. Gravity has forced electrons and protons together into
neutrons, and the object is held up by neutron degeneracy pressure.

```
mass      1.4 to 3 solar masses
diameter  about 20 km
density   a sugar cube's worth weighs as much as a mountain
```

Two properties come from conservation laws applied to the collapse. Angular momentum is
conserved, so a core that rotated once a month spins hundreds of times a second once it is 20
km across. Magnetic flux is conserved, so the field is amplified to a trillion times Earth's.

Together those produce a **pulsar**. The magnetic axis is tilted from the rotation axis, and
radiation beams out along the magnetic poles, sweeping past Earth once per rotation like a
lighthouse. The first was found in 1967 as a signal so regular it was briefly labelled LGM-1
for little green men, and the regularity is now used as a clock precise enough to detect
orbiting planets and to test general relativity in binary pulsar systems.

Above about 3 solar masses no known pressure resists gravity, and the result is a
[[Black Hole]].
